hero.headline: Demolition begins at Indian River Mall in Vero Beach to make way for mixed-use development
hero.teaser: Crews began tearing down portions of the Indian River Mall this week as the first phase of a major revitalization project gets underway. The Macys building is coming down now, with the former Sears location scheduled for demolition next.
hero.body:
Demolition crews began taking down portions of the Indian River Mall this week as part of a revitalization project. Project manager Joseph Scarfone said the first phase includes demolishing the Macy's building and the former Sears location. Neighbors gathered in the parking lot to watch, with many expressing relief about the change.

Mary Alice Stopyra said she was happy to see the building come down because it had degraded over time. Mark Manera, a longtime visitor to the mall, described it as looking like a graveyard with a steady decline year after year. Scarfone said the site will be transformed into a new indoor and outdoor shopping center with approximately 300,000 square feet of retail, restaurants, and possible residential spaces. He hopes the first phase can be completed by 2027, though crews are still working on permitting for the rest of the project.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie woman sentenced to 3 years in prison for running illegal med spa out of backyard shed
cards.body:
Rosa Mena, 50, of Port St. Lucie has been sentenced to three years in prison and five years of probation for operating an unlicensed medical spa out of a shed behind her home. Mena ran the business, called Miracle Hand and Spa, from her residence in the 5000 block of Northwest Coosa Drive. She was convicted on multiple charges including three counts of aggravated battery causing bodily harm, three counts of practicing medicine without an active license, and fraud charges.

The investigation began in May 2025 when a victim reported partial facial paralysis after receiving 62 units of Botox injections from Mena. The victim, who had been referred to the business by coworkers, paid $325 for the services. When the paralysis persisted, Mena offered to inject vitamins to reverse the issues and refunded the money. The victim requested to see Mena's medical license, and Mena provided an altered phlebotomy certificate that had actually expired in February 2024. Mena also claimed to be a doctor from the Dominican Republic.

Port St. Lucie Police, along with PSL Code Enforcement, the PSL Building Department, PSL Business Tax, and the Florida Department of Health, executed a search warrant at Mena's residence. Detectives discovered extensive medical equipment including medical beds, fat sculpting machines, laser hair removal equipment, laser liposuction machines, and injection devices for fillers and Botox. The equipment and evidence confirmed Mena had been operating a full medical spa operation without proper licensing or medical credentials.

The case highlights the dangers of unlicensed medical procedures and the consequences for those who operate illegal healthcare businesses. Port St. Lucie authorities worked across multiple agencies to investigate and prosecute Mena, who now faces three years behind bars followed by five years of supervised probation. The charges included use of a two-way communication device to facilitate a felony, fraud-swindle to obtain property valued at $300 or more, and fraud-swindle to obtain property under $20,000.

cards.headline: Jupiter Island officials say town is prepared despite state report warning of 9 feet of flooding at emergency center
cards.teaser: Jupiter Island leaders say they are well prepared for future storms even after a state vulnerability assessment identified 103 critical town assets at risk of flooding, including the town's Emergency Operations Center which could see up to 9 feet of floodwater.
cards.body:
Jupiter Island officials say they are "pretty well covered" for future storms following a new vulnerability assessment by the Florida Department of Environmental Protection. The report identified 103 critical town assets at risk of flooding, including 68 stormwater facilities, 17 historic sites, conservation lands, and key evacuation routes. The assessment warned that the town's Emergency Operations Center could see up to 9 feet of floodwater during severe weather events.

Jupiter Island Commissioner Marshall Field said the findings confirm what town leaders already knew, which is why they requested the assessment. Beach District Director John Duchok said the vulnerability assessment will serve as a roadmap for adaptation, allowing the town to tackle highest priorities first. Field said evacuation orders would be issued well before floodwaters threaten roadways and that the town has a backup facility on the mainland to maintain operations during emergencies.

cards.headline: Florida homestead tax exemption proposal could increase local fees, experts say
cards.teaser: A property tax cut proposal that would increase the homestead exemption from $50,000 to $250,000 over two years could lead to higher local fees and costs, according to experts weighing the potential impacts.
cards.body:
Florida lawmakers on Tuesday passed a property tax cut proposal that would increase the homestead exemption from $50,000 to $250,000 over two years, with inflation adjustments beginning in 2029. The bill requires approval from 60% of voters in November. The measure would also lower assessment caps on non-homesteaded properties from 10% to 5%.

Experts disagree on the consequences. Real estate attorney Steve Wallace said counties and local governments could impose new non-ad valorem taxes on sheriff's offices and fire rescue services, or increase fees to offset lost revenue. CPA Paul Miller suggested businesses could carry more of the financial burden through annual fees. Municipal attorney Raul Gastesi predicted home prices could rise as buyers have more money available. Danielle Blake, Chief of Residential Advocacy at MIAMI REALTORS + RWorld, disagreed, citing interest rates as the primary barrier to home sales rather than property taxes.

cards.headline: 12 Make-A-Wish children sworn in as junior deputies at St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office
cards.teaser: Sheriff Richard Del Toro swore in 12 children from the Make-A-Wish Foundation as junior deputies on Wednesday, calling it one of the greatest days of his career. The children toured the facility, saw K-9 and SWAT demonstrations, and received badges.
cards.body:
Twelve children from the Make-A-Wish Foundation were sworn in as junior deputies by St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro on Wednesday. Del Toro called it one of the greatest days in his career. The junior deputies received badges, toured the facility, and watched demonstrations from the helicopter, SWAT team, and K-9 unit.

Among the newest junior deputies were twins Mia and Daryl Nyack. In 2023, Mia was diagnosed with aplastic anemia, a blood disorder requiring a bone marrow transplant. Her twin brother Daryl donated his bone marrow to save her life. Mia said she was scared but her brother made her feel safe. Another junior deputy, Tobias Deleon, was diagnosed with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia in 2022. His mother, Charity Deleon, thanked the Sheriff's Office for welcoming their children into the community and reminding them they're important.

The extradition marks a significant development in a case that has remained unsolved for more than four decades. Authorities in Florida worked with Elkhart County investigators to locate and arrest the suspect, who was then transported back to face prosecution.

Cold case investigations have gained renewed attention in recent years as advances in forensic technology and DNA analysis have allowed law enforcement to revisit unsolved crimes from decades past. The 1981 homicide case had remained open as investigators continued to follow leads and review evidence. The decision to charge and extradite a suspect suggests that new evidence or witness testimony may have emerged to support prosecution.

The extradition from Florida highlights the interstate cooperation required to bring suspects to justice, even in cases that are more than 40 years old. Family members of the victim may finally see resolution in a case that has haunted them for decades.

Pulte Homes is marketing new residential developments in St. Lucie County to South Florida buyers looking for more affordable housing options. The national homebuilder is positioning the county as a bargain alternative for buyers priced out of markets to the south.

The move reflects St. Lucie County's growing appeal as a destination for residents seeking lower housing costs while remaining within reasonable reach of South Florida job centers and amenities. Pulte, one of the nation's largest homebuilders, is specifically targeting buyers who find traditional South Florida markets increasingly out of reach.

The development strategy comes as St. Lucie County continues to experience residential growth, with builders viewing the area as an opportunity to serve buyers migrating from higher-cost regions. The county has seen steady population increases in recent years as housing affordability challenges persist in Palm Beach, Broward, and Miami-Dade counties.

Pulte's focus on St. Lucie County adds to the momentum of residential construction activity across the Treasure Coast, where builders have been responding to demand from both local buyers and those relocating from more expensive Florida markets. The company's marketing campaign highlights the county as an accessible option for South Florida residents seeking homeownership at lower price points.

An heiress has acquired eight acres of land in Florida with the explicit goal of blocking development on the property. The purchase represents a conservation effort to maintain the land in its current state and prevent residential or commercial construction.

The transaction highlights growing interest among private individuals in preserving undeveloped land in Florida, where development pressure continues across many counties. Conservation purchases by private buyers have become an increasingly common strategy to protect natural areas from being converted to developed uses.

The eight-acre parcel will be preserved rather than built upon, removing it from the pool of property available for future housing or commercial projects. Such purchases by conservation-minded individuals complement public land preservation efforts and reflect concerns about the pace of development across the state.

The addition of behavioral health services addresses growing demand for mental health and substance abuse treatment across the region. MorseLife's expansion reflects increasing recognition of the need for integrated care that addresses both physical and mental health needs, particularly among senior populations.

A school board approved the closure and merger of county middle schools in a split vote. The decision came after debate among board members about the best way to serve students and use district resources.

School consolidations typically arise from declining enrollment, budget pressures, or efforts to improve educational offerings by combining resources. Middle school mergers affect students during a critical developmental period and require careful planning for transportation, staffing, and program transitions.

The split vote indicates disagreement among board members about whether consolidation serves the best interests of students and communities. Parents and staff at affected schools often have strong opinions about closures, which can disrupt established programs and community connections.

cards.headline: Bluffton senior prank involved 85 students, police identify main offenders
cards.teaser: Police say 85 students participated in a senior prank that turned into a disaster, though three were identified as the main offenders.
cards.body:
A senior prank at a Bluffton school involved 85 students, but police identified three as the main offenders responsible for what authorities described as a disaster. The large-scale incident required law enforcement investigation to determine who led the planning and execution.

Senior pranks are traditional end-of-year activities at many high schools, but they occasionally cross the line into vandalism or disruption that requires intervention. When pranks cause property damage or create safety concerns, school administrators and police must respond to hold students accountable.

The distinction between the three main offenders and the larger group of participants suggests varying levels of involvement and responsibility. Schools typically face difficult decisions about discipline when large numbers of students participate in pranks, balancing the desire to let seniors celebrate with the need to maintain order and protect school property.

cards.headline: Martin County schools police chief arrested for DUI
cards.body:
The police chief for Martin County schools was arrested on DUI charges this week. The arrest represents a significant development for the district's law enforcement leadership.

The schools police chief oversees safety and security operations across all Martin County school campuses. The position carries responsibility for protecting students, staff, and visitors at district facilities throughout the county.

Martin County schools serve thousands of students across elementary, middle, and high schools in Stuart, Jensen Beach, Palm City, Hobe Sound, and surrounding communities. The district employs its own police force to maintain security on school grounds and at school events.

The school district has not announced whether the police chief will remain in the position or what interim security arrangements might be made during the legal proceedings. The arrest comes at the end of the school year as districts prepare for summer operations.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Mets sweep doubleheader at Clover Park, take six-game series against Threshers
hero.body:
The St. Lucie Mets swept a doubleheader against the Clearwater Threshers on Wednesday at Clover Park, capping a six-game series between the two Florida State League teams. The Threshers came away with victories in both games of the twin bill, demonstrating their strength in the extended series matchup.

The series between the Mets and Threshers stretched across six days at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie, providing local baseball fans with multiple opportunities to watch Florida State League action. Tuesday's scheduled game was postponed, but the teams made up ground with Wednesday's doubleheader.

In Florida Complex League play on Tuesday, the FCL Mets fell to the FCL Nationals by a final score of 7-6. The Complex League provides developmental opportunities for younger players in the Mets organization who are working their way up through the minor league system.

The St. Lucie Mets continue their season at Clover Park as part of the Florida State League's competitive landscape. Minor League Baseball teams across the system are celebrating PLAY BALL Weekend in 2026, promoting youth baseball participation and community engagement throughout the sport.

cards.headline: Readers can vote for Treasure Coast's all-time best girls basketball players
cards.teaser: A poll is now open for Treasure Coast sports fans to vote on the area's all-time best players from girls basketball history.
cards.body:
Treasure Coast residents can now participate in voting to determine the all-time best girls basketball players from the local area. The poll allows fans to recognize outstanding athletes who have competed at schools across Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties over the years.

The voting initiative celebrates the legacy of girls basketball on the Treasure Coast and highlights the talented athletes who have represented local high schools in competition. The poll provides an opportunity for the community to honor players who have made significant contributions to the sport in the region.

Girls basketball has a strong tradition across Treasure Coast high schools, with many players going on to compete at the collegiate level. The voting process allows longtime fans and community members to reflect on memorable performances and championship seasons from past decades.

cards.headline: FCL Mets fall to FCL Nationals 7-6 in Florida Complex League action
cards.teaser: The Florida Complex League Mets dropped a close game to the FCL Nationals on Tuesday, losing 7-6 in developmental league play.
cards.body:
The FCL Mets came up short against the FCL Nationals on Tuesday, falling by a final score of 7-6 in Florida Complex League competition. The one-run game showcased competitive play between the two developmental squads as part of the complex league schedule.

The Florida Complex League serves as an entry-level professional circuit for players beginning their minor league careers. The FCL Mets provide Treasure Coast baseball fans an opportunity to watch future prospects develop their skills before potentially moving up to higher levels of the New York Mets farm system.

Complex league games typically feature younger players recently signed by major league organizations, including international signees and draft picks. The level represents the foundation of player development within professional baseball's minor league structure.

cards.headline: Tuesday rainout forces Mets-Threshers doubleheader at Clover Park
cards.teaser: Rain forced the postponement of Tuesday's scheduled game between the St. Lucie Mets and Clearwater Threshers, leading to Wednesday's doubleheader.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets and Clearwater Threshers saw their Tuesday game at Clover Park postponed due to weather conditions. The rainout forced a makeup doubleheader on Wednesday as part of the six-game series between the two Florida State League clubs.

The Threshers swept the Mets in the doubleheader on Wednesday, taking both games of the scheduled doubleheader.

cards.headline: Minor League Baseball celebrates PLAY BALL Weekend across the country
cards.teaser: Clubs throughout Minor League Baseball, including Treasure Coast teams, are participating in PLAY BALL Weekend 2026 to promote youth baseball.
cards.body:
Minor League Baseball teams across the nation are celebrating PLAY BALL Weekend in 2026, with clubs hosting special events and activities to encourage youth participation in baseball and softball. The initiative brings together professional teams at all levels to promote America's pastime to the next generation of players.

The PLAY BALL program represents Major League Baseball's umbrella initiative for youth baseball and softball participation. Minor league teams serve as community ambassadors for the program, hosting clinics, youth games, and interactive events at their ballparks throughout the weekend.

Treasure Coast baseball fans can expect to see PLAY BALL Weekend activities at local minor league facilities. The weekend-long celebration emphasizes accessibility and fun, introducing young people to baseball through hands-on experiences at professional ballparks.

cards.headline: Florida Complex League standings updated as developmental season continues
cards.teaser: The Florida Complex League has released updated standings as teams continue their developmental schedules in professional baseball's entry-level circuit.
cards.body:
Updated standings for the Florida Complex League show teams progressing through their 2026 schedules in the developmental circuit that operates across Florida training facilities. The FCL provides the first professional experience for many young players in their organizational journeys.

The Florida Complex League operates during the summer months at spring training facilities throughout the state. Teams play abbreviated schedules focused primarily on player development rather than competitive standings, though games are tracked and statistics maintained.

Treasure Coast residents with interest in the New York Mets organization can follow the FCL Mets as prospects work their way through the system. The complex league level represents the starting point for international signees and recent draft picks before they advance to full-season minor league affiliates.

cards.headline: Daytona Tortugas first half standings show Florida State League competition
cards.teaser: The Daytona Tortugas' first half standings have been released, showing the competitive landscape in the Florida State League's northern division.
cards.body:
First half standings for the Daytona Tortugas reflect the Cincinnati Reds affiliate's position in Florida State League competition as the season reaches its midpoint. The Florida State League divides its season into two halves, with playoff positioning determined by performance in each segment.

The Daytona Tortugas compete in the same league as the St. Lucie Mets, providing a regional connection for Treasure Coast baseball fans. Teams in the Florida State League represent the Single-A level of minor league baseball, one step above the complex leagues and one below High-A affiliates.

Florida State League teams play a full-season schedule from April through September, with the all-star break serving as the dividing line between the first and second halves. The league's structure allows more teams to remain in playoff contention throughout the summer.

hero.headline: Beetlejuice musical runs through June 7 at Kravis Center in West Palm Beach
hero.teaser: The Broadway hit musical Beetlejuice brings spooky humor and over-the-top visuals to the Kravis Center, with performances through June 7 at the Alexander W. Dreyfoos Concert Hall.
hero.body:
Beetlejuice the musical has landed at the Kravis Center in West Palm Beach, running June 2 through June 7. The Broadway hit brings spooky humor, over-the-top visuals, and heartwarming moments to Palm Beach County. Actor Ryan Stajmiger plays the mischievous demon in the iconic striped suit, a character beloved from Tim Burton's 1988 film. The musical follows Lydia Deetz, a strange and unusual teen whose life changes after meeting two recently deceased neighbors and a demon with a flair for trouble.

Stajmiger says one of his favorite parts is breaking the fourth wall to communicate directly with the audience. During an early performance, he experienced an unexpected moment when a wig change went wrong and he performed an entire scene bald. Performances include 7:30 p.m. shows on June 3 and 4, 8 p.m. on June 5, matinee and evening shows on June 6, and a closing matinee on June 7. Tickets start at $34.50 at kravis.org. The show is recommended for ages 13 and up.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast Fourth of July guide ready for America's 250th birthday celebration
cards.teaser: A complete guide to Independence Day events across the Treasure Coast is now available as communities prepare to celebrate America's 250th birthday this year.
cards.body:
Treasure Coast residents can access a complete Fourth of July guide for America's 250th birthday celebration. The milestone year marks a quarter millennium since the founding of the United States, and communities across Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties are preparing special events.

The guide provides details on fireworks displays, parades, festivals, and other Independence Day activities happening throughout the region. With the historic 250th anniversary adding significance to this year's celebration, local governments and organizations are planning enhanced programming for residents and visitors.

The guide helps families plan their holiday by providing information on locations, times, and special activities at various venues across the Treasure Coast. Residents can find events in Stuart, Port St. Lucie, Fort Pierce, Vero Beach, Sebastian, and other local communities.

cards.headline: Five public golf courses on Treasure Coast offer good prices and variety for players
cards.teaser: Golfers on the Treasure Coast have access to five public golf courses offering a range of prices and skill levels for players across the region.
cards.body:
Five public golf courses on the Treasure Coast provide options for golfers seeking good prices and courses suited to different playing levels. The courses serve residents and visitors across Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties who want accessible golf without private club membership.

The courses offer variety in both pricing and difficulty, allowing players to choose facilities that match their budget and skill level. Public courses provide an important recreational resource for the community, giving residents opportunities for exercise, social interaction, and outdoor activity throughout the year.

The availability of multiple public courses helps make golf accessible to a broader range of Treasure Coast residents. The facilities support both casual weekend golfers and more serious players looking for quality courses at reasonable rates.

cards.headline: Florida law on Fourth of July fireworks use explained ahead of holiday
cards.teaser: Florida residents wondering about the legality of setting off fireworks on Independence Day can review state law ahead of the Fourth of July holiday.
cards.body:
Questions about whether it is legal to set off fireworks on the Fourth of July in Florida are being addressed as the holiday approaches. State law governs when and how residents can legally use consumer fireworks, and understanding these rules helps prevent citations and promotes safety.

Florida law allows consumer fireworks on specific holidays, including Independence Day, but restrictions and local ordinances may apply. Residents should understand both state regulations and any additional rules set by their county or municipality before purchasing and using fireworks.

With America's 250th birthday this year, fireworks use may be more widespread than usual. Knowing the legal parameters helps residents celebrate safely and responsibly while avoiding potential fines or legal issues. Fire safety officials also recommend following manufacturer instructions and keeping water or fire extinguishers nearby when using any fireworks.

cards.headline: Jeopardy features Florida county grapefruit in $2,000 question
cards.teaser: A Florida county's grapefruit was featured as the subject of a $2,000 question on the popular game show Jeopardy.
cards.body:
Grapefruit from a Florida county was featured as a $2,000 question on Jeopardy, bringing national attention to the region's citrus industry. The game show question highlighted the county's reputation for producing quality grapefruit, which has long been an important agricultural product for Florida.

The Jeopardy appearance represents valuable publicity for Florida's citrus growers, who have faced challenges in recent years from hurricanes, disease, and changing markets. Recognition on a nationally broadcast program watched by millions of viewers helps promote awareness of Florida grapefruit and the state's agricultural heritage.

Citrus production remains an important part of Florida's economy and cultural identity, though the industry has contracted significantly from its peak decades. Features like the Jeopardy question help remind consumers about Florida citrus and may boost sales for growers working to sustain the industry.

cards.headline: Best spots for watching Palm Beach County Fourth of July fireworks identified
cards.teaser: Prime viewing locations for Fourth of July fireworks displays across Palm Beach County have been identified to help residents plan their Independence Day celebrations.
cards.body:
Residents looking for the best spots to watch Fourth of July fireworks in Palm Beach County now have guidance on optimal viewing locations. With America's 250th birthday adding special significance to this year's Independence Day, many families are planning where to watch fireworks displays across the region.

Good viewing locations allow families to see fireworks clearly while avoiding crowds and parking challenges that can make the experience less enjoyable. Knowing the best spots ahead of time helps residents arrive early enough to secure parking and set up comfortable viewing areas.

Palm Beach County typically offers multiple fireworks displays on Independence Day, giving residents options based on their location and preferences. Planning ahead ensures families can make the most of the holiday celebration and witness the spectacular displays marking this historic milestone year.

cards.headline: Lake Worth Beach to host finish of 80-mile ocean paddle for Crossing for Cystic Fibrosis
cards.body:
More than 100 paddlers will cross 80 miles of the open Atlantic Ocean this June to raise awareness and funds for families living with cystic fibrosis in the annual Crossing for Cystic Fibrosis. According to event founder Travis Suit, participants will launch from Bimini, Bahamas, at midnight on June 13, arriving at Lake Worth Beach after 12 to 16 hours of paddling. The endurance trek benefits the Pipers Angels Foundation, which Suit established in honor of his daughter, Piper, diagnosed with cystic fibrosis at age 4.

The crossing is part of a four-day schedule beginning June 10 with arrivals and a poolside social at Bimini Cove. Thursday brings a 4Ocean beach cleanup and a community buffet dinner. Friday features a Paddle Out Rose Ceremony to honor cystic fibrosis warriors, followed by rest and safety checks before launch night. All paddlers are required to wear a U.S. Coast Guard-approved personal flotation device, waterproof whistle, and reflective gear during dark hours. GPS trackers provided by the event must be worn and active at all times, and mandatory safety meetings will be held.

Paddlers must raise at least $2,000 for the cause, while crew or virtual participants have a $500 minimum. Final contributions are due July 31. Suit, an avid paddler, was inspired to create the event after learning about the natural respiratory benefits of ocean salt air. The foundation has since grown to provide direct support for cystic fibrosis patients and families, connecting them with resources and community.

Spectators are invited to Lake Worth Beach on June 13 to cheer paddlers during a daylong beach celebration marking their arrival. Cystic fibrosis is a life-shortening genetic condition that affects the lungs and digestive system. More information, registration, and donation details are available at crossingforcysticfibrosis.com and pipersangels.org.

hero.headline: Florida Bar and Courts Work to Address Rising Threats Against State Judges
hero.body:
The Florida Bar is working to address an increasing problem of threats against judges across the state. The professional organization that regulates attorneys in Florida has made addressing judicial security and threats against the judiciary a priority.

The effort comes as judges in Florida face growing security concerns in their courtrooms and communities. Threats against judges can undermine the independence of the judicial system and create an atmosphere of intimidation that affects the administration of justice throughout the state. The Florida Bar's involvement signals recognition that protecting judges is essential to maintaining a functioning court system for all Floridians.

The initiative reflects broader concerns about the safety of judicial officers as they carry out their constitutional duties. Judges make decisions in criminal cases, civil disputes, family law matters, and other proceedings that affect millions of Florida residents. When judges face threats or intimidation, it can compromise their ability to render impartial decisions based solely on the law and facts. The Florida Bar has positioned this work as part of its mission of pursuing justice, promoting professionalism, and protecting the public.

The Florida Bar announced the effort on June 4, 2026, as one of its top stories. The organization oversees attorney conduct, provides continuing legal education, and works on issues affecting the legal profession and justice system in Florida. While the announcement did not detail specific threat incidents or proposed solutions, the Bar's public focus on the issue indicates that judicial security has become a significant concern for legal professionals and court administrators statewide. Florida judges serve at all levels of the state court system, from county courts handling smaller matters to circuit courts, district courts of appeal, and the Florida Supreme Court.

cards.headline: Tampa Approves School Zone Speed Cameras as 6,000 Drivers Caught in Two Days
cards.teaser: Tampa City Council voted to authorize automated speed detection systems in 18 school zones after cameras caught 6,000 speeders in just two days.
cards.body:
Tampa City Council members voted Thursday to approve an ordinance to operate automated speed detection systems in 18 school zones throughout the city. The decision follows a two-day demonstration that caught 6,000 speeding violations in a single school zone.

Drivers caught exceeding speed limits in designated school zones will face $100 fines. The automated cameras can operate without constant police presence, potentially allowing law enforcement to focus on other duties while creating a deterrent effect in areas where children cross streets and walk to school.

cards.headline: Florida International University Research Shows Trees Shield Homes from Storm Damage
cards.teaser: Researchers at Florida International University have found that trees can provide protective benefits to homes during storms, offering new insights for hurricane preparedness.
cards.body:
Researchers at Florida International University have discovered that trees can shield homes from storms. A study at the Wall of Wind showed that trees around a low-rise building can reduce wind force on building segments by as much as 50%.

The findings have significant implications for Florida, a state that faces regular hurricane threats. The research could influence landscaping decisions, building codes, and urban planning across the state as homeowners and policymakers seek ways to reduce storm damage and lower insurance costs.

cards.headline: Florida Humidity Expected to Drop Temporarily Across State
cards.teaser: Florida's characteristic humidity is taking a short break, offering residents temporary relief from the moisture that typically blankets the state.
cards.body:
Florida's humidity is taking a short vacation, according to weather forecasters, providing temporary relief for residents accustomed to the state's typically moisture-laden air. The drier conditions represent an unusual respite from the subtropical and tropical climate that defines much of Florida.

The state's humidity typically remains high year-round, particularly during summer months when moisture from the Gulf of Mexico and Atlantic Ocean combines with warm temperatures to create muggy conditions. Lower humidity can make outdoor activities more comfortable and reduce the heat index, which measures how hot it actually feels when humidity is factored into the temperature.

The temporary reduction in humidity was reported on June 4, 2026, though weather patterns in Florida can shift quickly. Residents have likely noticed the difference in comfort levels, particularly during morning and evening hours when humidity often peaks. The break in typical conditions offers a reminder of how significantly moisture in the air affects daily life in Florida, from outdoor work to recreational activities to energy costs for air conditioning.

cards.headline: Florida Gators Pitcher King Named Finalist for College Baseball Foundation Award
cards.teaser: The College Baseball Foundation has named Florida Gators pitcher King as a finalist for Pitcher of the Year honors.
cards.body:
The College Baseball Foundation has named Florida Gators pitcher King as a Pitcher of the Year finalist, recognizing one of the top collegiate pitchers in the nation. The honor highlights both individual achievement and the strength of the University of Florida baseball program.

King's selection as a finalist places him among the elite pitchers in college baseball this season. The College Baseball Foundation recognition comes as college baseball programs complete their seasons and honors are distributed to standout players. For Florida Gators fans and University of Florida supporters, the nomination represents continued excellence in one of the school's premier athletic programs.

The University of Florida announced King's finalist status on June 4, 2026. College baseball has a strong following in Florida, where warm weather allows for year-round play and development of talent. The state produces numerous professional baseball players and hosts successful college programs at multiple universities. King's recognition adds to Florida's reputation as a baseball talent pipeline and reinforces the Gators' position among top college baseball programs nationally.

cards.headline: North Central Florida Veterans Build Community While Remembering Those Lost to Mental Health Struggles
cards.teaser: Veterans in North Central Florida are creating supportive communities while honoring the memory of those lost to mental health challenges.
cards.body:
Veterans in North Central Florida are building community connections while remembering those lost to mental health struggles, creating networks of support and remembrance. The effort addresses the ongoing challenge of veteran mental health and suicide prevention, issues that affect military veterans throughout Florida and the nation.

Mental health concerns remain a significant challenge for veterans transitioning to civilian life or coping with service-related trauma. By creating community and honoring those who have died, North Central Florida veterans are working to reduce isolation and provide mutual support. These grassroots efforts complement formal mental health services and veterans' programs offered by government agencies and nonprofit organizations.

The community-building work was reported on June 4, 2026. Florida is home to more than 1.5 million veterans, one of the largest veteran populations in the United States. Veterans Affairs facilities, veterans service organizations, and community groups across the state provide various forms of support, but peer connections often play a crucial role in helping veterans navigate challenges and find purpose after military service.

cards.headline: Florida State University Graduates First Leon County Cohort from Veteran Entrepreneurship Program
cards.teaser: Florida State University has graduated the first Leon County cohort from its veteran entrepreneurship program, helping former service members build business skills.
cards.body:
Florida State University has graduated the first Leon County cohort from its veteran entrepreneurship program, marking a milestone for the initiative designed to help veterans transition into business ownership. The program provides veterans with training, mentorship, and resources to start and operate their own businesses.

Entrepreneurship programs offer veterans an alternative career path after military service, allowing them to apply leadership skills and discipline gained in the armed forces to civilian business ventures. Florida State University's program joins similar efforts at universities and organizations across Florida and the nation to support veteran economic success. Leon County, home to Tallahassee and Florida State University, has a significant veteran population due to military installations and the state capital's role as a hub for veterans services.

Florida State University announced the graduation of the first Leon County cohort on June 4, 2026. The program's expansion to serve veterans specifically in Leon County suggests growing demand for entrepreneurship education among former service members. As veterans face challenges in the job market or seek independence through business ownership, programs like this one provide structured pathways to economic self-sufficiency and community contribution.

hero.headline: Person Airlifted with Traumatic Injuries After SUV Collides with Semi on I-95 in Martin County
hero.body:
One person was airlifted from the scene of a crash on Interstate 95 in Martin County after an SUV collided with a semi-truck Thursday. The victim suffered traumatic injuries in the wreck, which occurred on the heavily traveled interstate corridor that runs through the county.

The crash caused significant traffic disruptions on I-95, a critical route for local commuters and travelers moving through Martin County. Emergency responders worked at the scene to transport the injured person by helicopter to receive urgent medical care.

Details about what caused the collision between the SUV and semi-truck have not been released. The incident adds to ongoing concerns about highway safety on I-95, which sees frequent crashes involving both passenger vehicles and commercial trucks.

Motorists who regularly use I-95 through Martin County should expect potential delays as crash investigation and cleanup continue. The condition of the airlifted person and whether anyone else was injured in the wreck has not been disclosed by authorities.

cards.headline: All Lanes Closed on I-95 North Near Kanner Highway in Martin County After Crash
cards.teaser: A crash shut down all northbound lanes of Interstate 95 near Kanner Highway in Martin County early Thursday, blocking a major route for morning commuters.
cards.body:
All lanes of Interstate 95 North were closed near Kanner Highway in Martin County following a crash Thursday morning. The closure created a complete blockage of the northbound interstate at one of the county's key highway interchanges.

Kanner Highway serves as an important east-west connector in Martin County, linking communities from the coast inland. The crash site near this intersection meant drivers heading north on I-95 faced major delays and had to seek alternate routes during what would typically be morning rush hour.

Authorities have not released information about injuries or how many vehicles were involved in the crash. The complete lane closure on the northbound side of I-95 represents one of the more significant traffic disruptions Martin County drivers can face, as the interstate serves as the primary north-south corridor through the region.

cards.headline: Jupiter Island Says It's 'Pretty Well Covered' Despite Warning of 9 Feet of Flooding at Emergency Operations Center
cards.teaser: Jupiter Island leaders say they are prepared for future storms even as a new state vulnerability assessment warns the town's Emergency Operations Center could see up to 9 feet of floodwater.
cards.body:
Jupiter Island leaders say they are "pretty well covered" for future storms following a vulnerability assessment by the Florida Department of Environmental Protection. The report identified 103 critical town assets at risk of flooding, including 68 stormwater facilities, 17 historic sites, conservation lands, and key evacuation routes. The town's Emergency Operations Center could face up to 9 feet of floodwater.

Commissioner Marshall Field said the findings confirm what town leaders already knew, which is why they requested the assessment. The vulnerability assessment will create a roadmap for adaptation, allowing the town to prioritize improvements. Field said Jupiter Island plans to compete for state and federal funding to address vulnerabilities and will apply for a funding window that opened June 1. He noted that evacuation orders would be issued well before floodwaters threaten roadways and the town has a backup facility on the mainland to maintain operations during emergencies.

cards.headline: Martin County Beach Receives National Restoration Award
cards.teaser: A beach restoration project in Martin County has earned national recognition for its success in improving coastal conditions.
cards.body:
A Martin County beach has won a national restoration award, recognizing successful efforts to improve and protect the county's coastline. The award highlights the effectiveness of the restoration work completed at the beach site.

Beach restoration has been a priority for Martin County as erosion and storm damage threaten coastal areas. The recognition comes as communities throughout Florida grapple with the ongoing challenge of maintaining beaches that serve both as natural storm barriers and important recreational assets for residents and visitors.

The national award puts Martin County's coastal management efforts in the spotlight and may help the county compete for additional funding for future beach projects. Protecting beaches remains crucial for Martin County, where coastal property and tourism form significant parts of the local economy.

cards.headline: Wire 3 Plans $53 Million Investment to Power Up Three Martin County Communities
cards.teaser: Wire 3 has announced a $53 million investment to bring expanded power infrastructure to three communities in Martin County.
cards.body:
Wire 3 is investing $53 million to expand power infrastructure serving three Martin County communities. The substantial investment will upgrade electrical systems and ensure reliable power delivery to growing areas of the county.

The project represents one of the larger infrastructure investments in Martin County in recent years. Reliable electrical service is essential as the county continues to see residential and commercial growth, putting increased demands on the existing power grid.

The three communities that will benefit from the Wire 3 investment have not been specified in available information, but the scope of the project suggests significant construction work and system improvements ahead. County residents in the affected areas can expect to see enhanced power reliability and capacity once the infrastructure upgrades are complete.

cards.headline: Heiress Buying 8 Acres in Florida to Preserve Land from Development
cards.teaser: An heiress is purchasing 8 acres of Florida land with the goal of preserving it from future development.
cards.body:
An heiress has decided to buy 8 acres of land in Florida to protect it from development. The purchase is aimed at conservation, keeping the property in its natural state rather than allowing it to be converted to residential or commercial use.

Land preservation has become increasingly important in Florida as development pressure continues across the state. Treasure Coast communities have seen rapid growth in recent years, with natural areas giving way to new housing developments and commercial projects. Private conservation purchases like this one help maintain green space and protect wildlife habitat.

The specific location of the 8-acre parcel and the identity of the buyer have not been disclosed. Conservation-minded land purchases by private individuals and organizations provide an alternative to public land acquisition programs, which often face funding constraints and political challenges.

cards.headline: Florida Nuclear Power Plant Testing 91 Emergency Sirens Today
cards.teaser: Residents near a Florida nuclear power plant will hear emergency warning sirens being tested today as part of regular safety procedures.
cards.body:
A Florida nuclear power plant is testing 91 emergency sirens on June 4. The test is part of routine safety procedures designed to ensure the warning system functions properly in case of an actual emergency at the nuclear facility.

Residents living within range of the sirens should expect to hear the warning sounds during the test. The siren system is designed to alert people in surrounding communities if an incident at the nuclear plant requires protective action. Regular testing ensures the equipment works correctly and familiarizes residents with the sound of the warning signals.

Nuclear power plants are required to maintain and test emergency notification systems as part of federal safety regulations. The 91 sirens cover the emergency planning zone around the facility, which extends for miles in all directions from the plant site. Residents who hear the sirens during the test do not need to take any action, as it is a scheduled drill rather than an actual emergency.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County considering rocket recovery facility at Port of Fort Pierce
hero.teaser: County officials are evaluating a proposal to establish a rocket recovery facility at the Port of Fort Pierce.
hero.body:
St. Lucie County is considering a proposal to establish a rocket recovery facility at the Port of Fort Pierce. The facility would support the growing commercial space industry along Florida's Space Coast by providing infrastructure for recovering rocket components after launches.

The proposed facility represents a potential economic development opportunity for St. Lucie County and the Port of Fort Pierce, which has been working to expand its industrial and maritime operations. The space industry has grown significantly in Florida in recent years, creating new opportunities for coastal ports to serve launch operations.

County officials are reviewing the technical requirements and economic impact of the proposed facility. The Port of Fort Pierce's location and existing infrastructure make it a candidate for supporting space industry operations along the Treasure Coast.

cards.headline: Pulte Homes acquires 50 acres in Fort Pierce for Vela Cove development
cards.teaser: Pulte Homes has purchased a 50-acre site in Fort Pierce for a new residential development called Vela Cove.
cards.body:
Pulte Homes has acquired 50 acres in Fort Pierce for a new residential community called Vela Cove, targeting homebuyers looking for more affordable housing options in South Florida. The development represents a major investment in St. Lucie County's housing market as the region continues to experience growth.

The Fort Pierce location positions Pulte to serve buyers who are priced out of more expensive coastal markets but still want to live on the Treasure Coast. St. Lucie County has become an increasingly popular destination for families and retirees seeking lower housing costs compared to Palm Beach and Broward counties to the south.

The Vela Cove project will add to the inventory of new homes in St. Lucie County, which has been growing steadily in recent years. Details on the number of homes, price ranges and construction timeline have not been released.

cards.headline: Senator Ashley Moody honors Port St. Lucie Sgt. Levasseur with Florida's Finest Award
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie Sergeant Levasseur received the Florida's Finest Award from Senator Ashley Moody.
cards.body:
Senator Ashley Moody presented the Florida's Finest Award to Port St. Lucie Sergeant Levasseur in recognition of exceptional service to the community. The award honors law enforcement officers across Florida who demonstrate outstanding dedication and professionalism in their duties.

Sergeant Levasseur serves with the Port St. Lucie Police Department and was selected for the honor based on service to the community. The Florida's Finest Award is given to officers who exemplify the highest standards of law enforcement and make significant contributions to public safety.

The recognition highlights the work of local law enforcement in St. Lucie County and the dedication of officers who serve Port St. Lucie residents. Senator Moody, who previously served as Florida Attorney General, has made recognizing law enforcement a priority during her time in the Senate.

cards.headline: Funeral arrangements announced for St. Lucie County firefighter Connor Whitehead
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County community will honor fallen firefighter Connor Whitehead as funeral arrangements have been announced.
cards.body:
Funeral arrangements have been announced for St. Lucie County firefighter Connor Whitehead, who died in the line of duty. The services will allow the community to honor Whitehead's service and sacrifice to St. Lucie County residents.

Whitehead served as a firefighter with St. Lucie County Fire District, responding to emergencies throughout the county. His death marks a loss for the department and the community he served. The circumstances of his death reflect the dangers firefighters face while protecting residents.

The funeral will bring together firefighters from across Florida to honor their fallen brother. St. Lucie County Fire District and local officials are coordinating the services to ensure the community can pay respects to Whitehead and support his family during this time.

cards.headline: Three arrested overnight in Port St. Lucie police patrols
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie police arrested three people overnight in separate incidents ranging from shoplifting to DUI.
cards.body:
Three people were arrested during overnight patrols by Port St. Lucie police in incidents that included shoplifting and driving under the influence. The arrests came as officers conducted routine patrols throughout the city.

One arrest involved a DUI case that began as a domestic disturbance call. Police bodycam footage showed a driver attempting to dispose of a bag of marijuana during a traffic stop, which led to additional charges. The driver was taken into custody after failing field sobriety tests.

The arrests demonstrate the range of incidents Port St. Lucie police handle during overnight shifts, from property crimes to traffic enforcement. Officers continue to patrol neighborhoods and commercial areas throughout the city to maintain public safety.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie woman sentenced to 3 years in prison for running illegal med spa from backyard shed
cards.body:
Rosa Mena, 50, was sentenced to three years in prison and five years of probation after authorities discovered she operated an unlicensed medical spa called Miracle Hand and Spa from a shed behind her Port St. Lucie home. The case came to light in May 2025 when a victim reported partial facial paralysis after receiving 62 units of Botox injections from Mena at the makeshift facility in the 5000 block of Northwest Coosa Drive.

The victim, who had been referred by coworkers who previously used Mena's services, paid $325 for the procedure. When the victim reported the paralysis, Mena refunded the money but asked her to return for a vitamin injection to reverse the problems. After the paralysis continued, the victim requested to see Mena's medical license. Mena provided an altered phlebotomy certificate that had actually expired in February 2024. Mena also falsely claimed to be a doctor from the Dominican Republic.

A multi-agency investigation involving Port St. Lucie Police, PSL Code Enforcement, the PSL Building Department, the PSL Business Tax office and the Florida Department of Health led to a search warrant at Mena's residence. Detectives found medical beds, fat sculpting machines, laser hair removal equipment, laser liposuction machines and injection devices for fillers and Botox.

Mena was charged with three counts of aggravated battery causing bodily harm, three counts of practicing medicine without an active license, one count of fraud to obtain property valued at $300 or more, one count of fraud to obtain property under $20,000, and one count of using a two-way communication device to facilitate a felony. The investigation involved coordination between local code enforcement and state health officials to shut down the illegal operation.

cards.headline: 12 Make-A-Wish children sworn in as junior deputies by St. Lucie County Sheriff
cards.teaser: Sheriff Richard Del Toro honored 12 local children from the Make-A-Wish Foundation by swearing them in as junior deputies on Wednesday.
cards.body:
Twelve children from the Make-A-Wish Foundation were sworn in as junior deputies by St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro on Wednesday. The young honorees received badges, toured the sheriff's office, and watched demonstrations by the helicopter unit, SWAT team and K-9 units. "This is one of the greatest days in my career," Del Toro said.

Among the new junior deputies were twins Mia and Daryl Nyack. In 2023, Mia was diagnosed with aplastic anemia, a blood disorder requiring a bone marrow transplant. Her twin brother Daryl donated his bone marrow to save her life. Another junior deputy, Tobias, was honored alongside his mother Charity Deleon. In 2022, Tobias was diagnosed with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia and his heart stopped during treatment, but medical teams revived him and he recovered.

hero.headline: Indian River Mall demolition underway in Vero Beach for mixed-use development
hero.body:
Crews began tearing down portions of the Indian River Mall this week to make way for a revitalization project at the shopping center. Project manager Joseph Scarfone said crews are working on the first phase, taking down the Macys building and the former Sears location.

Neighbors gathered in the parking lot to watch the demolition. Mary Alice Stopyra, who lives nearby, said she is happy to see the mall torn down because it has degraded over time. Mark Manera from Vero Beach, who has been coming to the mall for years, said he saw a steady decline year after year. He described the struggling mall as more like a graveyard but believes the change is needed and could bring new life, new jobs, and new opportunity.

Scarfone said the site will be transformed into a new indoor and outdoor shopping center with around 300,000 square feet of retail, restaurants, and possible residential spaces. He described the vision as a city within a city, replacing a dead mall that had been collecting cobwebs for the last 12 years.

Scarfone said he hopes the first phase can be completed by 2027. The development team is still working on permitting for the remaining portions of the project.

cards.headline: New luxury apartments at The Vivien on Indian River Boulevard begin welcoming residents
cards.teaser: Ultraluxury apartments at The Vivien on Indian River Boulevard are starting to fill with tenants in Vero Beach.
cards.body:
The Vivien, a new ultraluxury apartment development on Indian River Boulevard in Vero Beach, is starting to welcome residents. The project brings high-end rental housing to the area along one of the community's main thoroughfares.

The development represents a significant addition to Vero Beach's residential market, offering premium apartment options for renters in the region.

cards.headline: Indian River County officials assess impact of Florida property tax proposal
cards.teaser: Indian River County is working to understand the scope of a new Florida property tax plan that could result in losses in the millions of dollars.
cards.body:
Indian River County officials are analyzing a Florida property tax plan that could significantly impact local government revenues. Counties across the state are working to understand the potential financial consequences, with losses projected to reach into the millions of dollars.

The proposal represents a major shift in how property taxes are collected and distributed in Florida. Local governments rely heavily on property tax revenue to fund essential services including schools, public safety, road maintenance, and other infrastructure.

County administrators are reviewing the details of the plan to determine how it would affect Indian River County's budget and ability to provide services to residents. The full scope of the impact is still being calculated as officials work through the complex changes proposed in the legislation.

cards.headline: Vero Beach pioneer to receive Florida historical marker recognition
cards.teaser: A Vero Beach pioneer will be honored with a Florida historical marker recognizing contributions to the community's history.
cards.body:
A Vero Beach pioneer is set to receive a Florida historical marker, honoring the individual's role in the development and history of the community. The marker will serve as a permanent recognition of the contributions made to the area.

Florida historical markers are awarded to commemorate significant people, places, and events that have shaped the state's history. The markers provide educational information for residents and visitors about important aspects of local heritage.

The recognition highlights Vero Beach's commitment to preserving and celebrating its history. The marker will join other historical designations throughout Indian River County that tell the story of the area's development and the people who helped build the community.

cards.headline: Florida family of five receives furnished home from nonprofits
cards.teaser: A Florida family of five has received a new furnished home with assistance from nonprofit organizations.
cards.body:
A family of five in Florida has been given a new furnished home through the efforts of nonprofit organizations working to help families in need. The home came fully furnished, providing the family with immediate housing and essential furnishings.

The collaboration between nonprofits demonstrates the work being done in Florida communities to address housing needs and support families facing difficult circumstances. The assistance included not just the home itself but also furniture and household items to help the family establish a stable living environment.

Nonprofit organizations throughout the Treasure Coast region work to provide housing assistance, furniture, and other support services to families struggling with homelessness or inadequate housing. These efforts help families achieve stability and work toward long-term self-sufficiency.

cards.headline: Summer vacation dates set for St. Lucie, Martin, and Indian River county schools
cards.teaser: School districts in St. Lucie, Martin, and Indian River counties have announced their summer vacation schedules.
cards.body:
School districts across the Treasure Coast have finalized their summer vacation dates for students in St. Lucie, Martin, and Indian River counties. The schedules provide families with the information needed to plan summer activities and childcare arrangements.

The summer break represents a significant period when students are out of school, affecting families, summer programs, and local businesses that rely on seasonal patterns. Parents and guardians use the information to coordinate work schedules and arrange for supervision and activities during the extended break.

School districts typically release these dates well in advance to allow families adequate planning time. The schedules also affect summer school programs, facility maintenance, and preparation for the upcoming academic year.

cards.headline: Community event focused on conversation, connection, and purpose held in Indian River County
cards.teaser: Residents gathered for an evening event centered on meaningful conversation and community connection.
cards.body:
An evening event bringing together community members for conversation, connection, and purpose took place in Indian River County. The gathering provided an opportunity for residents to engage in meaningful dialogue and build relationships with their neighbors.

Community events like this play an important role in strengthening local bonds and creating opportunities for residents to discuss issues that matter to them. The focus on conversation and connection reflects a growing interest in face-to-face interaction and community building.

The event represents one of many community gatherings held throughout the year in Indian River County that aim to bring people together around shared interests and values. Such events help foster a sense of community and provide forums for residents to connect beyond their daily routines.
